items.title: Kenya saves Ksh.1.5B as national examination papers printed locally
items.description: The national examination papers have printed locally for first time in 65 years, saving the country Ksh1.5 billion, President William Ruto has said.
content: The national examination papers have printed locally for first time in 65 years, saving the country Ksh1.5 billion, President William Ruto has said.

The announcement comes as a record 3.6 million learners the first ever largest cohort sat the Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA), Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) national assessments and Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) examinations which conclude this week.

Speaking during the State of the Nation Address at Parliament, Ruto questioned why the country had previously relied on overseas printing of examination papers despite having the capacity to print its own currency locally.
“The question I asked our ministry officials is this: If we are printing currency in Kenya, why can’t we print exams?” he posed.
He said the decision to print the papers locally had saved the country close to Ksh1.5 billion that would otherwise have been spent.
The President also said the examinations had been conducted in a calm and orderly environment without the intimidating security deployments witnessed in previous years.

“The examinations have been conducted in a calm and orderly atmosphere, free from the anxiety, tension and intimidating security deployments of the past. This is how it should be. Examinations are a normal part of learning, not a security operation or a matter of life and death. They should assess our children’s progress, not instil fear about their future,” said Ruto.

On teacher recruitment, Ruto said the government had employed 100,000 teachers over the past four years and planned to recruit an additional 20,000 next month to address staffing shortages and strengthen learning.
He said the investment in education was aimed at easing the financial burden on parents while ensuring learners had access to adequate teachers and quality learning facilities.

The government has also built 23,000 classrooms and is constructing and equipping 1,600 laboratories to expand access to learning and reduce pressure on communities to finance essential school infrastructure.
The President further announced that the national education allocation had increased from Ksh521 billion in the 2022/2023 financial year to KSh784 billion in the current financial year.
He said the resources must reach schools promptly and be managed responsibly, warning that parents should not be required to shoulder public education obligations through unauthorised charges.

“Our objective is to make education accessible and affordable while preparing children for better income opportunities. Every child who remains in school, acquires useful skills and enters productive employment strengthens both the household and the nation. Investment in education is also an investment in addressing the cost of living,” Ruto said.

The President described education as one of the most powerful instruments for equalising opportunities, saying the government was addressing inequalities in access to quality education through teacher recruitment, classroom construction and expanded student accommodation.

On higher education funding, Ruto said the government had initially reformed the funding model to provide greater support to students from less privileged families but acknowledged that tuition costs remained a barrier for many.

“In higher education, we initially reformed funding to provide greater support to students from less privileged families. But we recognised that even with this support, tuition costs still remained a barrier for many,” he said.
He said the government had consequently proposed further reforms through the Tertiary Education, Placement and Funding Bill, 2026, currently before Parliament.

Under the proposed legislation, no student admitted to a university, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution or Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) would miss classes because their parents could not afford tuition fees.

“We have therefore gone further. Under the Tertiary Education, Placement and Funding Bill, 2026 before this Parliament, we are proposing that going forward, no student admitted to our universities, TVET institutions or Kenya Medical Training Colleges will miss class on account of inability of their parents to pay,” Ruto said.

Archbishop Muheria threatens to sack church officials over politicians
items.description: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 18 – Nyeri Catholic Archbishop Anthony Muheria has threatened to sack church officials who allow politicians to address congregations, warning that anyone who turns a church into…
content: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 18 – Nyeri Catholic Archbishop Anthony Muheria has threatened to sack church officials who allow politicians to address congregations, warning that anyone who turns a church into a political platform will face immediate consequences.
Muheria issued the warning as the Catholic Church steps up its campaign to keep politicians from using places of worship to advance their political ambitions ahead of the 2027 General Election.
The Archbishop warned that priests, catechists, coordinators and church secretaries who facilitate political speeches during church services risk losing their positions.
“Whoever allows a leader, anyone among you who allows anybody to speak in the church, will be fired immediately,” Muheria declared.
He specifically warned church officials against arranging opportunities for politicians to address worshippers, saying those found responsible would be replaced.

items.title: Ruto takes veiled swipe at Gachagua over Mt Kenya voting bloc politics
items.description: Ruto challenged political leaders against asking entire regions to surrender their political choices to individual personalities.
content: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto has taken a veiled swipe at former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua over his political mobilisation in the Mt Kenya region, declaring that no community should be reduced to a voting bloc.

In his State of the Nation Address to Parliament on Wednesday, Ruto challenged political leaders against asking entire regions to surrender their political choices to individual personalities, insisting that voters should assess leaders on their proposals and performance.
“No community should be reduced to a voting bloc. No region should be asked to surrender its judgement to a personality,” he said.

Although he did not mention Gachagua by name, the remarks came amid the former Deputy President’s efforts to consolidate the Mt Kenya region behind his Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), which he has increasingly presented as an alternative political home for the region.
Gachagua has repeatedly described Mt Kenya as a DCP stronghold and urged residents to reject the ruling party and incumbent lawmakers allied to it, whom he has branded “traitors”.

Catholic Officials Who Allow Politicians to Speak in Church to Be Fired, Archbishop Muheria Says
items.description: Nyeri Archbishop Anthony Muheria threatened to fire Catholic church officials who allow politicians to address congregations during church services.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

Nyeri Catholic Archbishop Anthony Muheria has threatened to dismiss church officials who allow politicians to address congregations during services, warning that anyone facilitating political speeches will immediately lose their position.
Muheria issued the stern warning amid growing concerns over politicians turning religious gatherings into campaign platforms ahead of the 2027 General Election.
Speaking in Nyeri, the archbishop said the punishment would apply to all church officials, including coordinators, secretaries, catechists and other people entrusted with managing church activities.
He warned that anyone who handed a politician the microphone to address worshippers would face immediate dismissal once the matter was reported to him.

He added that the church would organise elections to replace officials removed for violating the directive.

The archbishop also condemned politicians who engage in heated exchanges and use obscene language inside churches, arguing that such behaviour undermines the sanctity of places of worship, particularly when children are present.
In a stern warning delivered in Kiswahili, Muheria insisted that churches belonged to God and should not be turned into political battlegrounds.

He further instructed worshippers to resist attempts by politicians to deliver political speeches during services, urging them to make noise and ululate whenever a politician is handed the microphone.

Muheria maintained that political leaders had other avenues to communicate their agendas, including public rallies and other political gatherings, instead of using churches to advance their ambitions.

The warning follows a nationwide directive issued by the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB) on Thursday, November 12, prohibiting politicians from delivering political addresses in Catholic churches ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The bishops maintained that churches should remain places of prayer, unity and spiritual nourishment where Kenyans from different political backgrounds can worship without being subjected to partisan campaigns.
They also reminded politicians that they had several alternative platforms to reach voters, including the media, public barazas and roadside rallies.

items.title: UK Embassy Kenya Announces Deadline for 2027 Fully Funded Commonwealth Scholarships Applications
items.description: Kenyan graduates can apply for 2027 Commonwealth Shared Scholarships, funding UK master's tuition, travel and living costs. Eligibility and 8 December deadline.

Kenyan graduates seeking postgraduate education in the United Kingdom have until December 8, 2026, to apply for fully funded master's degrees under the 2027 Commonwealth Shared Scholarships programme.
The British High Commission in Kenya publicised the opening of applications on November 18, 2026, through its official X account.
The programme is jointly funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and participating UK universities.

The award is designed specifically for talented candidates from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford postgraduate study in the UK. It typically runs for 12 months, covering an eligible one-year master's programme.

Six development themes anchor the 2027 awards: science and technology, population health, innovation and entrepreneurship, peace and governance, crisis resilience, and access and inclusion.
Approved courses span institutions including King's College London, the London School of Economics, the University of Edinburgh, and Sheffield Hallam University, among others.

After the December 8 deadline, participating universities will review candidates and forward nominations to the commission in March 2027.
Selection weighs academic merit, the quality of the study proposal, and the potential development impact on Kenya following the scholar's return home.
Scholars are required to return to Kenya within one month of completing their studies and cannot use the award as a pathway to remain in the UK for employment.
The scholarship does not automatically cover costs for accompanying dependants.

The United Nations has opened applications for its 2026 Young Professionals Programme (YPP), offering entry-level professional positions in Development and Sustainability at the P-1 and P-2 grades across several UN duty stations, including Nairobi.
The application deadline is 30 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. New York time.
The YPP is the UN Secretariat's primary recruitment pathway for early-career professionals seeking to serve as international civil servants.

The programme combines an entrance examination with structured professional development and is open exclusively to nationals of countries that are unrepresented or under-represented within the Secretariat.

The list of eligible countries shifts each year.
Five African nations are included in the 2026 cycle: Angola, Equatorial Guinea, Liberia, Libya, and São Tomé and Príncipe.

Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa , and Ethiopia do not appear on the list, making their nationals ineligible to apply through the standard nationality-based route this year.

Kenyans who hold dual nationality with one of the qualifying countries may still be considered, provided they enter that nationality in the "Country of Nationality" field and attach a government-issued photo ID confirming it.
The UN has clarified that nationality at birth and other secondary nationalities are not taken into account for YPP eligibility.

To qualify, candidates must be nationals of a participating Member State, hold at least a bachelor's degree in a relevant field, be 32 years old or younger during the examination year, meaning born on or after January 1, 1994, and demonstrate proficiency in English or French at UN Level II or above.

Prior work experience is not mandatory, though it may be used to rank applicants when large volumes of applications are received from a single country.
The 2026 examination covers economics, statistics, social affairs, environmental issues, sustainable development, technology and digital transformation, and programme management support.
Assessment proceeds in three stages: application screening, a written examination, and an oral interview.
The written exam is split into two parts, with Part I tentatively scheduled for February 2027 and the oral stage anticipated for mid-2027.
Candidates placed on the resulting roster are eligible to fill vacancies across the UN Secretariat for three years, though placement does not guarantee appointment.
Those offered positions receive a two-year fixed-term contract, with the possibility of a continuing contract subject to satisfactory performance.
Kenyans who are ineligible this cycle are encouraged to monitor future editions of the programme, as the participating country list is revised annually.
Alternative entry routes into the UN system include the UN Volunteers programme, junior professional officer schemes, internships, and mid-level vacancies open to all Member State nationals.

items.title: Saudi Arabia Reveals Jobs Kenyans Can Apply for Under New Labour Deal
items.description: Saudi Arabia clarifies Kenya labour annex covers only domestic workers and private drivers, while 293,600 job opportunities remain separate and unsigned.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development has clarified that the technical annex signed with Kenya on November 12, 2026, applies exclusively to domestic workers and private drivers.
The ministry confirmed the agreement does not cover skilled professionals in healthcare, construction, education, or any other sector.

The Saudi government urged the public to depend solely on its official channels for recruitment information, a move widely interpreted as a response to what it regards as inflated characterisations of the deal's scope.
The annex was signed in Riyadh by Deputy Minister of Human Resources and Social Development for Labour Abdullah Abuthnain and Cabinet Secretary Alfred Nganga Mutua.

PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
It builds on a bilateral domestic worker recruitment agreement the two countries concluded on July 5, 2026.

The annex rests on three pillars: lowering recruitment costs, raising the quality of domestic workers through training and qualification programmes, and protecting the rights of all parties in the contractual relationship.
A separate letter of intent also established a three-month pilot programme on voluntary recruitment fees, designed to keep Kenya competitive against other labour-sending countries.

During and after his Riyadh visit, Mutua announced that Saudi employment agencies had committed to 293,600 job opportunities for Kenyans spanning healthcare, construction, hospitality, education, transport, manufacturing, finance, oil and gas, and domestic work.
He also said both governments had agreed that their technical teams would conclude a separate skilled workers recruitment framework within one month.
Those announcements described intentions and future negotiations rather than the contents of the signed document.
The Saudi clarification, issued on November 17, draws a firm distinction between the binding domestic worker annex and the broader discussions on skilled labour that remain unresolved.
3 big changes US companies hiring green card holders must know
No specific salary rates or a revised minimum wage for Kenyan workers have been agreed upon, and the promised skilled workers agreement has not yet been signed.
Notably, the 293,600 job commitments were made by recruitment agencies and private companies, not incorporated into the annex.
Without a signed skilled workers agreement, the framework needed to channel Kenyans into those professional roles does not yet exist.
For Kenyans in domestic work and private driving, the annex represents a tangible improvement: streamlined recruitment procedures, reduced costs, and stronger contractual protections.
Pre-departure training programmes are also set to be strengthened to better prepare workers before they depart.
For those seeking professional roles, the Saudi government has confirmed no agreement is currently in place.
Kenyans who have been approached with offers of skilled employment in Saudi Arabia before a formal framework is concluded should treat such offers with caution.

Mutua separately noted that Kenya had engaged Saudi authorities regarding travel restrictions linked to reported Ebola cases, stating that the case had been identified and isolated with no community transmission recorded.
The Saudi ministry's statement did not address the travel restrictions.

items.title: Nairobi health facilities triple revenue to Sh2.6bn: City Hall
items.description: The county is targeting Sh4 billion in health facility revenue in the current financial year as it expands access to healthcare.
content: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — Revenue from Nairobi County health facilities has tripled from Sh800 million to Sh2.6 billion after digital reforms and improved reimbursements under the Social Health Authority (SHA), Governor Sakaja Johnson said.

The county is targeting Sh4 billion in health facility revenue in the current financial year as it expands access to healthcare, strengthens primary health services and invests in hospital infrastructure.

Speaking at the Third Annual Nairobi Health Scientific Conference, Sakaja attributed the growth to reforms under SHA, Facility Improvement Financing, improved claims management and enhanced accountability at facility level.
He said the additional resources enabled public hospitals to procure medicines, strengthen diagnostic services, maintain equipment, and support community outreach programmes.

“We have registered three million people in Nairobi under the Social Health Authority (SHA), representing more than 60 per cent of the city’s population. SHA has been working well in Nairobi, enabling us to serve more residents through the reimbursement of claims for services provided,” Sakaja said.

items.title: OPINION: Bayern vs Ajax: A grand spectacle for Kenya, but are our priorities right?
items.description: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 – The announcement that German giants Bayern Munich and Dutch powerhouse Ajax will face off in Nairobi on January 5, 2027, to inaugurate the newly built…
content: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 – The announcement that German giants Bayern Munich and Dutch powerhouse Ajax will face off in Nairobi on January 5, 2027, to inaugurate the newly built Raila Odinga International Stadium is undoubtedly exciting news for Kenyan football.
It is an opportunity to showcase our sporting infrastructure, attract international attention and build momentum ahead of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) 2027.
However, beyond the prestige of hosting two European football giants, I believe there are bigger questions that need to be asked.
Are we investing in the right priorities, and who is this historic occasion really being organised for?

Bringing clubs of Bayern and Ajax’s stature to Kenya comes at a significant cost. While the government has indicated that corporate partners would help facilitate the event, there is still a need for greater clarity on who these partners are, their financial contributions and how the entire arrangement is structured.

items.title: AFCON 2027: The nine countries already qualified for the tournament
items.description: The first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
content: The first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya , Tanzania and Uganda .
With four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. Here are all the countries that have qualified.

After the three host nations, who qualify automatically although they are taking part in the qualifiers, the fourth matchday of the 2027 qualifying campaign revealed six new qualified teams on 17 November 2026.

The co-host of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is having a very mixed qualifying campaign. Benni McCarthy’s side did snatch a good point in South Africa (2-2), but they have only two points after four matchdays and had a scare at home against modest Eritrea (1-1).

Of the three host nations, Uganda are undoubtedly the ones having the best qualifying campaign, and the only ones to have won a match, a 1-0 victory over Libya. They are unbeaten after four matchdays and top their group ahead of Libya, Botswana and Tunisia.

The last of these automatically qualified nations, Tanzania have not necessarily made a strong impression. They have only two points after four matchdays, but they have just held Nigeria to a 0-0 draw, their best performance of the campaign so far.
One by one, the spots are being claimed! Here's who's qualified for #TotalEnergiesAFCON2027 after Matchday 4. ? https://t.co/uUJmkEBOVX

While waiting for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule on their status as 2025 champions or finalists, Senegal became the first team to secure their place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on the pitch. After a laboured start in Mozambique (1-1), Patrick Vieira’s side strung together three wins, over Ethiopia and then Sudan twice, to confirm their ticket 24 hours after their matchday four game, thanks to a favourable result for Mozambique.

Held by Benin (1-1) in their opening game, Burkina Faso, round of 16 finalists in the last two editions, then dropped no more points, beating Central African Republic and then Mauritania twice. Amir Abdou’s side needed only four matchdays to qualify.

Round of 16 finalists in 2025, Benin will be present again for the Pamoja edition. After taking a good point from their trip to Burkina Faso (1-1), Gernot Rohr’s side dictated terms to Mauritania and then Central African Republic twice to secure qualification in November 2026, following Burkina Faso’s win over Mauritania.

After reaching the quarter-finals of the previous edition, Cameroon are taking these qualifiers very seriously. Held only in Congo, David Pagou’s side beat Comoros and Namibia twice to qualify after four matchdays, following Congo’s 1-0 defeat to Comoros.

Keen to go further than the quarter-finals, the ceiling reached in the last two editions, Mali confirmed their ambitions by being the only team along with Morocco to maintain a perfect record after four matchdays. World Cup-bound Cape Verde, Liberia and Rwanda twice all fell to Anthony Da Silva’s side, who qualified thanks to these wins.

As formidable as ever in these qualifiers, Morocco have a perfect 4/4 record, having beaten Gabon, Lesotho and then Niger twice. It was the second win over Niger, 1-0, thanks to a record-breaking goal from Abdellah Ouazane, that allowed Mohamed Ouahbi’s side to qualify.

The content creator had been fighting a rare parasitic eye infection called Acanthamoeba Keratitis, a notoriously difficult condition to diagnose.
He previously revealed that he endured more than 14 medical tests before doctors could identify what was attacking his eye.

His wife, Miss Wanjey, shed more light on the situation during a TikTok livestream on November 11, explaining that the amoeba had burrowed into the cornea, where it forms cysts and keeps multiplying, making treatment extremely complicated.

She also disclosed that medical teams had been treating the wrong condition for close to two months, giving the infection a dangerous window to advance. That delay is what ultimately caused his left eye to turn visibly white and robbed him of all sight in it.
Baba Talisha has confirmed that surgery is on the horizon, and he is now preparing to travel to India for specialist medical attention.

items.description: TikTok creators revealed Mwai Kibaki's Othaya home in Nyeri, with its green-and-black gate, leafy grounds and lasting significance as a quiet place of remembrance.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!
Kenyans have caught a rare glimpse of the late President Mwai Kibaki's family home in Othaya, Nyeri County , after a group of TikTok content creators shared footage from their visit to the area.
The adventurers rode along a well-maintained tarmac road before passing the expansive compound, which sits in quiet, leafy surroundings typical of central Kenya's highlands.
From the roadside, the residence cuts an impressive figure. A large green and black gate with a roof-style design marks the main entrance, flanked by neat cabro paving and a security guard's chamber.
Jimi Wanjigi opens doors to his palatial compound during 64th birthday celebrations

The boundary is lined with tall trees and a green fence, with patches of yellow flowers providing bursts of colour. Banana trees tower above the perimeter, nodding to the agricultural character of the region.

The TikTokers did not venture inside the compound, but the exterior alone left a strong impression, conveying a sense of calm and comfort befitting a man who spent the better part of his life at the centre of Kenyan public affairs.

Kibaki served as Kenya's third president from 2002 to 2013. Born in 1931 in Gatuyaini village in Othaya, he maintained a deep connection to the area throughout his political career, having also represented the constituency in Parliament for many years.
He passed away on April 21, 2022, at the age of 90. A state funeral was held in his honour, and on April 30 he was laid to rest at the Othaya home with full military honours.

He was buried beside his wife, the late former first lady Lucy Kibaki, who died in April 2016 and was also interred at the family home.
Since both leaders were laid to rest there, the compound has quietly become a place of reflection for Kenyans who pass through or travel to the area specifically to pay their respects.
TUKO.co.ke also highlighted facts about Uhuru Kenyatta’s visit to Kabarak, where he paid tribute to Daniel arap Moi and his wife, and addressed the university’s graduands.
The visit gave Kenyans a glimpse of president Moi's final resting place .

Kenya’s female-led venture capital firm closes $26m fund to support African fintech startups
items.description: Kenya-based, pan-African female-led venture capital firm First Circle Capital has closed its Africa Fund I at $26 million, securing capital to invest in early-stage fintech startups developing the next generation of financial products, services and technology infrastructure across the continent. The fund will back startups at the pre-seed and seed stages, focusing on six key […]
content: Kenya-based, pan-African female-led venture capital firm First Circle Capital has closed its Africa Fund I at $26 million, securing capital to invest in early-stage fintech startups developing the next generation of financial products, services and technology infrastructure across the continent.

The fund will back startups at the pre-seed and seed stages, focusing on six key areas: insurance technology (insurtech), alternative lending models, financial interoperability and infrastructure, climate fintech, fintech software-as-a-service (SaaS), and regulatory technology (regtech).

First Circle Capital, which specialises in African fintech and has offices in Nairobi, Kampala, Casablanca and Cape Town, was founded by Selma Ribica, a former M-Pesa executive and fintech investor; Agnes Aistleitner, a serial entrepreneur with experience in emerging markets; and Robert Smith, a former strategy professional with a background in technology entrepreneurship in East Africa.

The firm’s investment strategy, which it describes as “FinTech 2.0”, seeks to build on the first generation of African fintech companies that transformed payments and lending by backing businesses addressing broader gaps in financial services.
These include expanding access to credit and insurance, strengthening financial infrastructure, improving digital business operations and enhancing regulatory compliance.

The firm is also placing greater emphasis on AI-native fintech startups, which integrate artificial intelligence, automation and data-driven operations into their businesses from inception. According to First Circle Capital, these technologies could reduce the cost of delivering financial services, improve product efficiency and enable companies to serve more customers.

“We are particularly excited by the emergence of AI-native fintech companies. Founders now have the opportunity to build financial businesses around automation, intelligence, and software from day one, fundamentally changing the economics of delivering financial services across African markets,” said Selma Ribica, Co-Founder and Managing Partner at First Circle Capital.
“We want to identify those businesses at the earliest stages and work closely with their founders as they scale.”

Africa Fund I has a pan-African investment mandate, targeting fintech opportunities in established and emerging markets, including Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Uganda, Ghana and Francophone Africa.

Investors in the fund include the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Bpifrance, MSMEDA, Axian, the Dutch Good Growth Fund, Stellar Foundation and FSD Africa. The fund brings together development finance institutions, institutional investors and strategic partners to support the firm’s investment strategy.

First Circle Capital has already invested in 18 companies across African markets, building a portfolio spanning payments, financial wellness, alternative lending, insurtech, climate finance, fintech SaaS, commerce enablement, card infrastructure and fraud prevention.

Some of its portfolio companies include South Africa-based TurnStay, which develops cross-border payment infrastructure for global travel merchants; Morocco’s WafR, which digitises transactions and payments through neighbourhood retailers; Scale, a Card-as-a-Service infrastructure provider; and Orca Fraud, which uses artificial intelligence to help financial institutions prevent fraud.

Other investments include Opareta, which provides software and data solutions for managing mobile money agent networks; Balad, an Egyptian regulated remittance infrastructure provider facilitating international money transfers; and Power, which offers earned wage access solutions to major African banks.

Beyond providing early-stage capital, First Circle Capital says it works closely with portfolio companies to help them secure follow-on funding, attract strategic investors, establish commercial partnerships and pursue business development opportunities. Several of its portfolio companies are now progressing towards Series A funding rounds.
Agnes Aistleitner, Co-Founder and Partner at First Circle Capital, said significant gaps remain in Africa’s financial services industry despite the growth of fintech businesses over the past decade.

“Despite the extraordinary growth of fintech across Africa over the past decade, significant gaps remain in key verticals such as financial access, interoperability, digital infrastructure, and the availability of specialised financial products,” she said.

Aistleitner added that the fund would support founders developing solutions to make payments cheaper, expand access to credit and insurance, strengthen fraud prevention and risk management, and improve financial operations through software.
She also pointed to opportunities in sectors such as agriculture and energy, where specialised financial solutions could address longstanding financing challenges.
Robert Smith, Partner and Head of Operations at First Circle Capital, said the firm’s ambition is to back companies that become central to the delivery of financial products across African markets.
“Our ambition with Africa Fund I is to build a portfolio of companies that become fundamental to how financial products are delivered across Africa,” Smith said.

He added that the next generation of African fintech businesses would combine local market knowledge with advanced technologies, including AI-native solutions, to improve the accessibility and economics of financial services.

With its $26 million fund now closed, First Circle Capital is positioning itself to back early-stage founders seeking to address structural challenges in Africa’s financial services sector, while supporting the development of technology-driven businesses across the continent.

items.title: Kenya Set To Sign Landmark Trade Agreement With Nigeria To Boost Technology Businesses
items.description: (3 Minutes Read)
content: Kenya is among five African countries expected to enter into a major trade agreement with Nigeria aimed at expanding cross-border operations for technology companies and strengthening digital trade across the continent. The proposed deal will allow Nigerian technology businesses to access new markets, establish operations and serve customers in participating countries, including Kenya.

The agreement will bring together six African economies: Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, South Africa and Egypt. Its signing is expected later this month during a meeting of the Council of Ministers of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) in Zimbabwe.

Nigeria’s Minister of Trade and Investment, Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed the development in an interview with Reuters , explaining that the five partner countries were selected following an assessment of markets where Nigerian digital businesses have significant growth potential.

According to Oduwole, the Nigerian government has already engaged regulatory authorities from the participating countries to identify barriers to cross-border business operations and establish a framework for greater cooperation. The consultations involved central banks, trade ministries and other institutions responsible for regulating digital businesses and facilitating trade. “We held a regulatory roundtable sandbox with those regulators, from their central banks to their ministries of trade to all the enablers,” Oduwole told Reuters .

The proposed agreement is expected to create opportunities for businesses operating in financial technology (fintech), digital payments, e-commerce and other technology-driven sectors. By improving regulatory cooperation and facilitating market access, the initiative seeks to make it easier for companies to expand their services beyond their domestic markets.

For Nigerian technology companies, Kenya and the other participating countries could provide access to new customers, business partnerships and investment opportunities. Similarly, Kenyan businesses could benefit from improved access to Nigeria’s large consumer market, potentially expanding opportunities for digital service providers, fintech firms and e-commerce platforms. The initiative could also strengthen commercial relationships between the participating countries by encouraging technology investment, promoting innovation and reducing some of the administrative and regulatory obstacles associated with operating across African borders.

The development comes against the backdrop of Kenya’s growing influence in Africa’s digital economy, particularly in e-commerce, financial technology and digital services. The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) has ranked Kenya as Africa’s third-largest e-commerce market, highlighting the country’s expanding online business ecosystem and increasing adoption of digital commerce.

Additionally, World Bank data identifies Kenya as the second-largest exporter of digital services in Sub-Saharan Africa. This position reflects the country’s growing capacity to provide technology-enabled services to international markets, supported by its established digital infrastructure, mobile financial services ecosystem and expanding technology sector. Greater access to Nigeria’s market could further strengthen Kenya’s digital businesses by creating opportunities for regional expansion, cross-border partnerships and increased revenue generation.

Despite the potential benefits, several details of the proposed agreement remain unclear. Oduwole did not disclose the specific provisions of the arrangement or explain whether it would immediately alter existing licensing, taxation or compliance requirements for foreign technology companies operating in the participating countries.

It is also yet to be established how the agreement will address differences in national regulatory frameworks, data protection requirements, digital payment regulations and other policies governing technology businesses across the six markets. The extent to which the proposed framework will simplify company registration, licensing and cross-border financial transactions will therefore become clearer once the agreement is formally signed and its implementation arrangements are announced.

Nevertheless, Nigeria says the initiative is part of a broader strategy to help African businesses expand across the continent rather than remain restricted to their domestic markets. “We’ve been pushing to support our businesses to do more on the continent. That’s the way we’re going to grow our economies,” Oduwole said.

The proposed agreement forms part of wider efforts under the African Continental Free Trade Area to deepen economic integration, increase intra-African trade and create a more favourable environment for businesses operating across national borders. Through the AfCFTA framework, African governments are seeking to reduce trade barriers, improve market access and encourage the movement of goods and services across the continent. Expanding cooperation in the digital economy is increasingly important as technology companies, online marketplaces and financial service providers play a growing role in economic development.

For Kenya, participation in the proposed arrangement could strengthen its position as a regional technology and digital services hub while providing local businesses with greater opportunities to compete in Africa’s largest consumer markets. If effectively implemented, the agreement could mark an important step towards building a more connected African digital economy, allowing technology companies to scale their operations, reach new customers and contribute to economic growth across the continent.

Duale reaffirms commitment to health reforms, accountability
items.description: Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale has announced the the introduction of a digital messaging system that enables patients to confirm receipt of prescribed medicines warning that SHA will not reimburse facilities for medicine claims where patients have not received their prescribed medication.
content: Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale has reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to vigilance, transparency and accountability in the response.

Speaking Wednesday when he represented President William Ruto at the official opening of the 3rd Annual Health Scientific Conference in Nairobi, Duale highlighted progress in ongoing health reforms, noting that the SHA has registered over 33 million Kenyans, representing 70 per cent of the population, and mobilised USD 1.9 billion since its inception.

He also announced the the introduction of a digital messaging system that enables patients to confirm receipt of prescribed medicines warning that Social Health Authority (SHA) will not reimburse facilities for medicine claims where patients have not received their prescribed medication.

Held under the theme, “One Health in Action: Building Resilient, Climate-Smart and Equitable Health Systems for UHC”, the three-day conference provides a platform for deliberations on health security and pandemic preparedness, urban health resilience, reproductive, maternal, child and adolescent health, nutrition, non-communicable diseases, mental health and digital health.

CS Duale called on county governments to strengthen health facilities and Primary Healthcare Networks, invest in healthcare workers through fair terms of service and constructive dialogue, and maximise the contribution of the more than 107,800 CHPs deployed nationwide.

“Nationwide, over 107,800 CHPs are connecting households to health facilities, supported by digital health reforms that will integrate patient records, referrals, claims processing and disease surveillance,” he said.
He further highlighted the role of digital health in strengthening patient management, referrals, claims processing and disease surveillance.

Similarly, he CS recognised Nairobi County’s partnership with the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) in strengthening urban health research and surveillance, alongside the enactment of the Health Services and Management Act, 2026, expansion of intensive care capacity from zero to 46 beds within three years and the ongoing construction of a cancer centre in Parklands.

On health security, the CS commended Nairobi County for its response to the imported Ebola case, noting that 923 healthcare workers and 1,598 Community Health Promoters (CHPs) were trained to support response efforts.

He confirmed that Kenya is on Day 7 of the 42-day countdown, with no new cases reported. Subject to continued surveillance and no further cases, the country is expected to be declared Ebola-free on 23 December 2026.

To improve maternal and newborn health outcomes, the Ministry is accelerating interventions under the Every Woman Every Newborn Everywhere (EWENE) initiative, complemented by the Rapid Results Initiative (RRI), with particular focus on the 26 high-burden counties.
Duale said plans are underway to expand cancer screening at the primary healthcare level to promote early detection, timely referral and treatment.
The CS was hosted by Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja and Deputy Governor James Njoroge, alongside development partners, conference delegates, county and Ministry of Health officials.

"I'll make sure illness is not a sentence to poverty" - President Ruto highlights Kenya's state of health care

content: President William Ruto took time to explain the state of healthcare in the country during his fourth State of the Nation Address in Parliament on Wednesday, November 18.

In his address, the Head of State noted that the Kenya Kwanza Administration has come-up with healthcare reforms through a system of shared health financing, rather than falling entirely on individuals and their family, to address the cost involved in medical treatment.

The President stated that so far, 33.7 million Kenyans had registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), comparing this to the National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) in 2022, where approximately 8 million Kenyans were beneficiaries.

“Under the former NHIF, only 8 million Kenyans were registered. Today, under SHA, that number stands at 33.7 million. That is 25.7 million more Kenyans brought into the national health financing system. Millions who were previously outside its protection, for whom illness could mean selling their land, exhausting their savings or sinking into debt,” President Ruto stated.

He further stated that across the country, 53, 465 patients are currently receiving cancer treatment, 24,468 patients are receiving dialysis, while 89 patients have undergone kidney transplant under SHA.
At the same time, he acknowledged that SHA has been facing challenges that the government is working hard to address.

“The transition to SHA had initial challenges and we recognised the legitimate concerns of Kenyans. We have consistently addressed those concerns because health protection must be experienced by citizens in practice as it’s promised in policy,” the President said.

Ideally, the President emphasised that his administration is working to progressively and eventually remove the crushing burden of medical expenses from Kenyan households, protect family savings and ensure that illness does not become a sentence to poverty.

The President went ahead and gave a testimony of a lady known as Veronica who is a beneficiary of SHA. He mentioned that by her contributing Ksh840, the government was able to cover her medical bill that exceeded KSh966,00.
The Head of State, reiterated that the insurance fund has enabled patients to gain access to health care without over burdening their families.

items.title: Ruto says SHA protecting families from financial burden of illness
items.description: President William Ruto has hailed healthcare reforms implemented by his administration through the Social Health Authority (SHA), saying families no longer have to bear the full cost of treatment on their own.
content: President William Ruto has hailed healthcare reforms implemented by his administration through the Social Health Authority (SHA), saying families no longer have to bear the full cost of treatment on their own.

Ruto said many families in the past have been forced to borrow money, sell livestock and land or abandon treatment altogether to meet medical costs, warning that illness can wipe out years of savings and push households into financial distress.
Speaking during his State of the Nation Address at Parliament Buildings on Wednesday, the President SHA has shifted the burden of medical expenses from households to a shared financing system.

“That is the burden we set out to lift through our healthcare reforms; To ensure that the cost of treatment is increasingly met through a system of shared health financing, rather than falling entirely on individuals and their families,” said Ruto.

“Our undertaking is to progressively and eventually remove the crushing burden of medical expenses from Kenyan households, protect family savings and ensure that illness does not become a sentence to poverty,” he added.
The President noted that 33.7 million Kenyans have so far registered under the scheme, compared with approximately eight million under the National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) in 2022.
He added that 53,465 patients were receiving cancer treatment, 24,468 were undergoing dialysis and 89 had undergone kidney transplants under SHA.

“Through SHA, covered treatment costs are being financed on behalf of patients, reducing the amounts that families would otherwise have to raise from their savings, seek or borrow from relatives, or obtain through the sale of their assets,” he said.
The President acknowledged that the transition from NHIF to SHA encountered initial challenges, saying the government recognised and continued addressing concerns raised by Kenyans.
He maintained that the success of the reforms will ultimately be measured by whether Kenyans can access the healthcare promised under the policy.
“Health protection must be experienced by citizens in practice, as promised in policy,” he said.
